posts.name: Rajat Raj Singh
posts.cooked:
Question

Conside a user User1 and the current working directory to be /home/User1/Dir1.

echo This displays '$PWD' and "$USERNAME"

The output of the above command is:

Options

  1. This displays /home/User1/Dir1 and User1
  2. This displays $PWD and User1
  3. This displays /home/User1/Dir1 and $USERNAME
  4. This displays $PWD and $USERNAME

Correct Answer

Output

This displays $PWD and

Explanation

$PWD enclosed inside single quotes would be printed literally. There exists no default environment variable named USERNAME. So, $USERNAME would print empty strings.

My Answer

Since there is no correct answer in the given options, I’ve chosen the 4th option, which is the closest to the correct one. @sayan Please look into it and kindly resolve the issue of deduction of marks for this question.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Rajat_Raj:

There exists no default environment variable named USERNAME.

This is incorrect.

In some distributions both USER and USERNAME are exported, whereas some distributions only export USER and USERNAME is undefined.

The question follows directly from the demonstration videos of that week where USERNAME has been clearly used and explained multiple times, so students are expected to answer (2).

posts.name: Rajat Raj Singh
posts.cooked: Ohk! Thank you. I basically read from the book that was referred to us & I use Linux Mint OS on my system. That’s why the doubt. Thanks for the clarification.
